content.comment_body: I have an [product_name] analog input module, an [product_name] analog output module, a [product_name] controller, and an [product_name] power supply 24V/4A. To connect the analog input module to the controller, should I use the side connector? Is it possible to connect the analog output module while the controller and input module are already connected, so that the controller can read both modules? If so, how can this be done?

One [product_name] controller with [version_no] can handle the following: 24 digital inputs, 20 digital outputs, 8 analog inputs, and 8 analog outputs. This is only possible if the expansion modules are attached at the same time. Is that clear? It's best to check the manual for your [product_name].
If I have two [product_name] analog input modules and two [product_name] analog output modules, does that mean only one of each can be connected to the controller via the side connectors?
Each expansion module includes an interlock slider and a connector on the right side. Please review the manual, especially chapter 2.2. You can download it here: [document]

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users are seeking guidance about connecting multiple expansion modules, such as analog input and RTD modules, to a controller system and whether several modules of each type can work together simultaneously. The discussion revolves around physical connection mechanisms like side connectors and interlock sliders, as well as system limitations for module quantity and addressing. Reference documentation is recommended but users still have questions about connectivity and expandability.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want to link multiple expansion modules (analog input and output modules) to a controller, aiming for simultaneous operation and the ability for the controller to read all attached modules.
